2013-06-11: Former Iranian presidents Mohammad Khatami and Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani publicly endorse moderate cleric Hassan Rouhani ahead of Friday's presidential election.
2013-06-14: Hassan Rouhani pledges to follow the path of moderation and justice, not extremism, in his first comments after winning Iran's presidential election.
Hassan Rouhani, a moderate cleric backed by reformists, appeared likely to advance to a runoff in Iran's presidential election amid high turnout and extended voting hours.
Hassan Rouhani wins Iran's presidential election.
2013-06-15: Hassan Rouhani wins Iran's presidential election, securing just over 50% of the vote to avoid a runoff and succeeding Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
2013-06-16: Hassan Rouhani's victory in Iran's presidential election boosted cautious hopes for a change in the country's troubled relations with the West, though ultimate power remains with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
2013-06-22: Hassan Rouhani was elected president of Iran, winning 18 million votes, three times as many as his nearest rival.
2013-06-29: Iran's president-elect Hassan Rouhani said his election victory was a mandate for change and vowed to remain committed to campaign promises of moderation and constructive engagement with the international community.
2013-07-02: Iran's president-elect Hassan Rouhani expressed relatively progressive views on civil liberties, freedom of expression, and the internet in an interview with the youth magazine Chelcheragh, opposing sex segregation, pledging to minimize censorship, and calling internet filtering futile.
2013-07-12: Hassan Rouhani's victory in Iran's presidential election was officially endorsed, prompting celebrations in Tehran.
2013-08-01: Iran dismisses a US House of Representatives sanctions bill that toughens measures over its nuclear programme, with critics saying the legislation could thwart diplomatic hopes following Hassan Rouhani's election victory.
2013-08-03: Hassan Rouhani is inaugurated as Iran's seventh president.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei formally endorses Hassan Rouhani as president, opening the way for him to take over from Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
2013-08-04: Hassan Rouhani is officially sworn in as Iran's new president, pledging moderation and urging dialogue based on mutual respect rather than sanctions.
Britain will not send a representative to Hassan Rouhani's inauguration despite an invitation from Tehran, with the EU agreeing that only Tehran-based diplomats would attend.
2013-08-06: Iran's new president Hassan Rouhani said his government is determined to engage in serious negotiations with the West to resolve the nuclear impasse and is open to direct talks with the US if Washington shows goodwill.
2013-08-15: Iran's conservative-dominated parliament approved 15 of Hassan Rouhani's 18 proposed cabinet ministers, including Mohammad Javad Zarif as foreign minister and Bijan Zanganeh as oil minister.
2013-09-12: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani transferred responsibility for nuclear negotiations with foreign nations from the Supreme National Security Council to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
2013-09-15: Barack Obama and Hassan Rouhani exchanged letters, setting the stage for a possible meeting at the UN, which would be the first face-to-face encounter between a US and Iranian leader since 1979.
2013-09-17: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei signaled that newly elected President Hassan Rouhani has the authority to conduct direct talks with the US and offer compromises in nuclear negotiations.
2013-09-18: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani stated in an NBC interview that Iran will never seek to build nuclear weapons and claimed his government has full authority to negotiate over its nuclear program.
2013-09-19: Signs indicate Iran's newly elected president Hassan Rouhani wants to break the stalemate over its nuclear programme and ease sanctions on its economy.
2013-09-20: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani called for "constructive interaction with the world" in an opinion article published by the Washington Post, signaling a softer stance ahead of a possible informal meeting with Barack Obama at the UN General Assembly.
2013-09-21: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani arrives in New York to address the UN General Assembly.
2013-09-24: A much-anticipated meeting between US President Barack Obama and Iranian President Hassan Rouhani did not happen, as White House officials said the Iranian delegation turned down the offer, calling it "too complicated."
2013-09-27: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani, at a press conference in New York, hails the US as "a great nation" and offers to prepare a concrete plan to resolve the nuclear stalemate at negotiations in Geneva on 15 October.
Iranian President Hassan Rouhani held a telephone conversation with US President Barack Obama, the first such presidential contact between the two countries since 1979.
2013-09-28: Hassan Rouhani returned to Tehran from New York after his historic phone call with Barack Obama, greeted by cheers from supporters and protests from hardliners who threw eggs and shoes at his car.
2013-10-05: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei says some of President Hassan Rouhani's diplomatic moves toward the United States during his New York trip were "not appropriate," while reiterating support for the new policy of outreach to the West.
2013-10-15: A new Iranian delegation under President Hassan Rouhani presented concrete proposals in Geneva on limiting Iran's nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief, in the first substantive nuclear negotiations since Rouhani's June election.
2013-11-04: Iranian hardliners held nationwide protests at the former US embassy in Tehran, highlighting domestic challenges Rouhani faces in his bid to mend ties with the West; Rouhani and his cabinet did not attend.
2013-11-08: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani's diplomatic efforts in Geneva face opposition from hardliners in Tehran, though his approach appears to have the backing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
2013-11-19: David Cameron spoke on the phone to Hassan Rouhani, becoming the first British prime minister to speak to an Iranian president in a decade.
2014-02-04: President Hassan Rouhani asked officials to study whether jamming satellite TV signals could pose a health risk, prompting Iran's health ministry to set up a committee to investigate.
2014-02-05: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani promised healthcare for all Iranians within four years, with at least five million uninsured citizens to be covered first.
2014-02-11: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani faces increased domestic opposition to his interim nuclear agreement with six world powers, with critics distributing leaflets and displaying placards during Islamic revolution anniversary rallies questioning whether his government made too many concessions.
2014-02-28: Six months into his presidency, Hassan Rouhani faces domestic pressure over unfulfilled economic and social reform promises, despite progress in international negotiations and some achievements such as currency stabilization.
2014-05-03: A newly formed group of Iranian MPs and rightwing activists called "We're Worried" criticizes Hassan Rouhani's government over the nuclear talks with the West.
2014-05-11: Iranian officials say the Ukraine crisis has strengthened Iran's position in nuclear talks, while President Hassan Rouhani stresses closer ties with Russia to mitigate sanctions.
2014-05-30: Prayer leaders in Tehran and Mashhad respond to President Hassan Rouhani's remarks about not forcing people to heaven, with hardline imams declaring they will stand against those who prevent people from going to heaven.
2014-06-14: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said Iran is seeking a nuclear deal with major world powers by the 20 July deadline and that the international sanctions regime had crumbled and would not be rebuilt even if no final deal is reached.
2014-07-13: Hassan Rouhani's first anniversary as Iranian president approaches, with his moderate mandate dependent on reaching a comprehensive nuclear deal in Vienna before the 20 July deadline.
2014-08-30: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said Iran should "resist" new US sanctions, calling them an "invasion of the Iranian nation," as the foreign ministry warned the measures would hinder nuclear talks.
2014-09-25: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani told the UN General Assembly that a nuclear agreement could clear the way for greater Iranian cooperation with the West on combating Islamist extremism, while saying regional powers should lead the fight against ISIS.
2014-11-12: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani urged the US to stop making “excessive demands” in nuclear negotiations, saying Iran had already made sufficient compromises ahead of talks in Vienna.
2014-11-14: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani's government is engaged in direct nuclear diplomacy with the US, with his negotiating team traveling to Vienna for a critical round of nuclear talks.
2015-02-03: Iran's parliament voted overwhelmingly to fast-track a bill that would require Hassan Rouhani's government to halt implementation of the interim nuclear agreement with the west if the US imposes further sanctions.
Iranian President Hassan Rouhani says a nuclear deal with the West is getting closer, stating that gaps have narrowed though some differences remain.
2015-03-18: Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian is reported to be caught in an internal feud between Iranian President Hassan Rouhani’s administration and hardliners, who accuse Rezaian of gaining privileged access through Rouhani’s nephew; Rouhani has maintained silence on the case.
2015-03-26: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani held a phone call with UK Prime Minister David Cameron in which they agreed international negotiators had a "historic opportunity" to reach a framework deal on Iran's nuclear programme.
2015-03-31: Negotiators from the US and Iran race toward a deadline for a comprehensive nuclear deal, which could transform the presidencies of Barack Obama and Hassan Rouhani.
2015-04-02: A nuclear deal was reached in Switzerland in which Iran, under President Hassan Rouhani, promised drastic cuts to its nuclear programme in return for the gradual lifting of sanctions.
2015-04-03: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said Iran will fulfill all its obligations under the historic nuclear framework agreement and hailed it as the start of a "new page" of cooperation with the international community.
2015-05-04: President Hassan Rouhani said that "Colt- and handcuff-toting agents of the regime" should not be expected to "act as religious scholars," returning to the issue of bad hijab and law enforcement in a speech before a group of teachers.
2015-05-12: A public opinion poll conducted 12-28 May indicates that a majority of Iranians support a nuclear agreement but high expectations for speedy sanctions relief could affect support for Hassan Rouhani's government ahead of the 2016 parliamentary election.
2015-05-26: President Hassan Rouhani unofficially kicked off next February's parliamentary elections before a gathering of provincial governors, calling for competitive elections and warning against improper interference by officials, the Revolutionary Guards, the military, media, or mosques.
2015-07-14: Hassan Rouhani is ranked as the biggest winner of the international nuclear agreement between Iran and six world powers, which ends Iran's international isolation and recognizes its right to peaceful nuclear energy.
2015-07-23: Activists and lawyers urge Iranian President Hassan Rouhani to focus on human rights after the nuclear deal, amid concerns over executions and other violations.
2015-09-25: President Hassan Rouhani said conditions were ripe for his administration to start implementing the July nuclear agreement by the end of the year.
2015-09-28: In his UN General Assembly speech, Hassan Rouhani criticized Saudi Arabia over the hajj crush, urged an independent investigation, and discussed the Iranian nuclear deal.
2015-09-29: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani did not meet face-to-face with US President Barack Obama in New York, though Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif shook hands with Obama at the UN General Assembly building.
2015-10-01: A survey by IranPoll.com for the University of Maryland finds that 89% of Iranians express favorable attitudes toward President Hassan Rouhani and three in four support the nuclear agreement.
2015-10-13: The Iranian parliament passed a bill approving the nuclear deal, a boost for Hassan Rouhani whose credibility was on the line had parliamentarians voted down the accord.
2015-10-21: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei gives qualified approval to the nuclear accord in a letter to President Hassan Rouhani, adding conditions that could complicate its implementation.
2015-12-31: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani accused the US of "illegal meddling" and ordered his defense minister to step up Iran's ballistic missile program in response to the prospect of new White House sanctions.
2016-01-16: Hassan Rouhani hailed a "glorious victory" after international sanctions against Iran were lifted following confirmation that Tehran had fulfilled its obligations under the nuclear accord.
2016-01-17: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said that 150 companies from 50 countries had recently visited Iran for investment following the lifting of sanctions.
2016-01-18: Following the lifting of sanctions after Iran's implementation of the nuclear agreement, President Hassan Rouhani again called for Iran to rely less on oil sales and to reform the economy, though analysis indicates significant economic reform is unlikely during the rest of his first presidential term.
2016-01-25: Hassan Rouhani is to make the first state visit to Europe by an Iranian president in almost two decades, starting in Rome and later traveling to Paris.
2016-02-26: Hassan Rouhani’s allies win a significant boost in Iran’s parliamentary and clerical assembly elections, strengthening his position to pursue further opening to the West and gradual domestic change.
2016-02-28: Reformist-backed candidates allied with President Hassan Rouhani won all 30 Tehran parliamentary seats and most Tehran assembly of experts seats in Iran's elections, seen as a boost to Rouhani.
2016-03-20: In his Nowruz speech, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei called for a "resistance economy" to fight unemployment and recession, differing in tone from President Hassan Rouhani's emphasis on attracting foreign investment and boosting the private sector.
2016-12-06: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani said Iran will not allow Donald Trump to tear up the nuclear deal and warned that extending US sanctions could violate the agreement.
2017-04-09: Conservative cleric Ebrahim Raisi announces his candidacy for Iran's presidential election, challenging moderate incumbent Hassan Rouhani.
2017-04-12: Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad registers to run in the upcoming presidential election, a move that could challenge incumbent Hassan Rouhani, who is expected to seek re-election.
2017-04-14: Hassan Rouhani registered to run for a second term as Iran's president.
2017-04-20: Iran’s Guardian Council approved Hassan Rouhani as one of six candidates to run in the country’s presidential elections, while disqualifying Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and more than 1,600 other nominees.
2017-05-02: Former President Mohammad Khatami endorses Hassan Rouhani for Iran's presidential election, saying Rouhani's continuation is in the country's best interests.
2017-05-14: Iranian film director Asghar Farhadi endorsed Hassan Rouhani for president ahead of Friday's vote.
2017-05-17: Hassan Rouhani campaigns in the final days before Iran's presidential election, locked in a close race against conservative cleric Ebrahim Raisi.
2017-05-19: Hassan Rouhani wins re-election as Iran's president in a landslide victory.
2017-06-22: Tensions mount between Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and President Hassan Rouhani after Rouhani's landslide re-election victory, with Khamenei sharpening his criticism and Rouhani asserting that a religious leader's political legitimacy derives from the people's will.
2017-06-23: Iran's president Hassan Rouhani was heckled during an annual pro-Palestinian rally in Tehran, with protesters comparing him to Abolhassan Banisadr, amid an escalating power struggle with the supreme leader.
2017-07-15: Hossein Fereidoun, brother and top aide of Iranian President Hassan Rouhani, was arrested after failing to secure bail on charges connected to financial crimes.
2017-08-05: Hassan Rouhani is sworn in for a second term as Iran's president, using the ceremony to criticize US President Donald Trump and reaffirm Iran's commitment to the nuclear deal.
